actions.action: Poke white spots with a cotton swab to confirm mealybugs (smear test)
Dab each bug with a cotton swab dipped in 70% isopropyl alcohol
Rinse the plant with a gentle shower in the sink, focusing on stem bases
Spray with insecticidal soap or neem oil every 5–7 days for 3–4 weeks
Repot outdoors or over newspaper, wearing gloves if desired
Check soil and roots for white fluff when repotting
If roots have mealybugs, rinse roots well and use fresh potting mix
Clean the old pot with soap or diluted bleach
Trim heavily infested stems and bag them for disposal
Keep plant quarantined for at least a month after bugs disappear

reason: The answer correctly identifies mealybugs and leads with 70% rubbing alcohol, matching the fix that worked, and its extra steps are not harmful.
